Subject: Reminder - Peter Schwerdtfeger Lecture Thursday 6th March


Hi Everyone

I would like to remind you of the Professorial Lecture  on Thursday, the
6th March presented by Professor Peter Schwerdtfeger, speaking on his
topic:

"Everything is relative" says Albert Einstein, and we chemists are
learning it the hard way!

Abstract:
Albert Einstein is well known as a physicist, so why should chemists be
interested in his work? The famous Einstein formula E=mc2 led to the
unification of two fundamental laws: the law of mass conservation in
chemistry and the even older law of energy conservation in physics.
Einstein must have known about this, but what he did not know is that
valence electrons of the heavy elements in the Periodic Table are
strongly influenced by relativistic effects, changing substantially
their underlying chemistry and physics. Hence Albert Einstein can now be
celebrated by chemists as well.

Staff, students and members of the public are welcome to this lecture.

Time:
7.00 Wine and Hors d'oeuvres
7.30pm Professorial Lecture

Where:
Sir Neil Waters Lecture Theatres Building, NW200.

If you have not already RSVP'd to this lecture, please do so for
catering purposes, by sending me an email: 

u.dgfphz@massey.ac.nz
